status: V1 testing preview with open release gates; V2 planning baseline 2026-10-25

phases.title: Product and architecture baseline
steps: Capture every requested capability and distinguish initial, later, and gated scope.
Document architecture, UX, data ownership, security, offline sync, and platform limits.
Create the repository map, 64 phase plans, phase evidence template, progress register, and documentation validator.
acceptance: All requested capabilities map to a phase and release gate.
A successor can select Phase 01 without needing chat history.
No skeleton directory is represented as implemented functionality.
checks: Run node scripts/validate-planning.mjs and inspect all failures.
Review naming clearance limitations, scope boundaries, source citations, and Git diff.
phases.commit: docs(planning): establish product architecture and phased roadmap

phases.title: Toolchain and executable workspace
steps: Pin a supported Node LTS and pnpm version; select an Expo SDK and compatible React/React Native versions, then validate Next.js package boundaries.
Replace reserved application READMEs with minimal runnable mobile, web, API, and worker workspaces and real package manifests.
Add strict shared TypeScript configuration, formatting, linting, and documented development commands without adding product features.
acceptance: A clean clone installs using the committed lockfile and documented commands.
Web and API smoke routes run; the mobile shell builds in an Expo development build.
Root lint, typecheck, test, and build commands exist and fail on intentional errors.
checks: Run clean install, lint, typecheck, available smoke tests, and each workspace build.
Record Windows development behavior and any Android SDK/device prerequisites.
phases.commit: chore(workspace): establish typed application and package toolchains

phases.title: Continuous checks and contributor automation
steps: Add pull-request checks for clean install, lint, types, planning validation, tests, and relevant builds.
Add dependency/secret scanning with an explicit exception process and protected deployment environments.
Create issue and PR templates; document branch protection setup when GitHub is connected.
acceptance: The workflow invokes actual scripts and grants minimal token permissions.
A failing contract or type check blocks a hosted PR once the remote is configured.
No deployment or billable provider account is required for contributor validation.
checks: Run the workflow commands locally; inspect permissions and cache inputs.
If a remote exists, record hosted CI run URLs; otherwise state hosted CI is pending.
phases.commit: chore(ci): enforce workspace quality and contribution checks

phases.title: Platform and integration feasibility spikes
steps: Use disposable prototypes to validate mobile SQLite, browser IndexedDB, auth session storage, and local-first navigation.
Measure Expo development-build support for notifications, secure storage, biometric prompts, recording, and selected crypto libraries.
Record constraints for Android exact alarms, browser notification support, Drive scopes, Play billing, and eventual iOS releases; replace assumptions with ADRs.
acceptance: Each high-risk capability has observed evidence or an explicitly recorded external prerequisite.
The team has a supported native build strategy rather than depending on Expo Go for all features.
Unavailable capabilities have honest UI fallback requirements and no guaranteed timing claim.
checks: Run device/browser experiments and record versions, permissions, and failure behavior.
Check current primary documentation and link it with the checked date.
phases.commit: docs(feasibility): validate platform constraints and implementation choices

phases.title: Design tokens and accessible primitives
steps: Encode the approved light/dark palette, typography, spacing, radii, focus treatment, and motion preferences as semantic tokens.
Implement a small set of buttons, fields, dialogs/sheets, feedback, and list row primitives separately for browser and native semantics.
Create a component review surface and include errors, disabled, loading, focus, large text, and right-to-left readiness.
acceptance: Text and control contrast meets the documented AA target in both themes.
Components are operable with keyboard or native screen reader and do not rely on color alone.
Touch targets, safe areas, reduced motion, and large text are reviewed on a real device.
checks: Run web accessibility checks, contrast calculations, and keyboard journeys.
Review native primitives with TalkBack and increased system font size.
phases.commit: feat(design): add accessible light and dark interface primitives

phases.title: Responsive web navigation shell
steps: Implement desktop sidebar, tablet transitions, and compact navigation using the documented information architecture.
Provide Today, Plan, Library, and Journal parent routes; place Calendar under Plan and Settings/Search/Create in consistent reachable controls. Include explicit empty/loading/error behavior.
Add browser shortcuts, focus restoration, deep-link handling, and responsive page containers; use synthetic content only.
acceptance: Navigation works at compact, tablet, and wide widths without horizontal clipping.
Back/forward and direct links preserve the expected location.
Keyboard focus and navigation labels are clear on every route.
checks: Run responsive browser smoke tests and keyboard navigation checks.
Inspect light/dark screenshots for hierarchy and readable density.
phases.commit: feat(web): add responsive organizer navigation

phases.title: Android navigation shell
steps: Implement tab/stack navigation, headers, safe areas, and capture entry points using native patterns.
Add route contracts for notifications, files, and authentication links.
Handle Android back navigation, keyboard avoidance, app resume, and reduced motion.
acceptance: A physical Android device can navigate every shell destination.
Small displays, system font scaling, and keyboard opening do not hide primary controls.
Deep links validate identifiers before routing and require appropriate authentication.
checks: Run Android development-build smoke journeys and navigation tests.
Inspect portrait/landscape and TalkBack behavior on supported screen sizes.
phases.commit: feat(mobile): add accessible Android organizer navigation

phases.title: PostgreSQL and tenant isolation foundation
steps: Define versioned migrations for profiles, workspaces, memberships, audit metadata, and shared item identities.

Implement least-privilege application DB access using a restricted non-owner runtime role, tenant-scoped queries, RLS for application tables, and private storage policies; verify the actual pooled connection role and transaction-local identity reset.
Create synthetic fixtures and repeatable local database setup; define migration ownership and hosted environment separation.
acceptance: Two users cannot read, update, enumerate, or reference each other's private workspace data.
Migrations reproduce a database from zero and support the chosen forward-fix workflow.
Service credentials remain server-side and cannot be read from client bundles.
checks: Run fresh/upgrade migration checks and cross-tenant RLS tests through the actual API/worker runtime role, including pooled connection identity reset.
Inspect role grants, foreign-key tenant consistency, and indexes for primary queries.
phases.commit: feat(database): establish workspace isolation and migration foundations

phases.title: API contracts and service foundation
steps: Add Fastify module registration, versioned REST routes, runtime request/response validation, and OpenAPI generation.
Implement JWT verification, membership authorization, structured redacted logging, request IDs, errors, limits, and health/readiness checks.
Generate or type the shared API client from canonical contracts and document pagination/cancellation.
acceptance: Unauthenticated and unauthorized requests fail consistently without leaking object existence.
Invalid input is rejected at the boundary and contract drift fails checks.
Health and readiness reveal operational state without secrets.
checks: Run route schema, expired token, authorization, rate-limit, and error contract tests.
Inspect representative logs for content and credential leakage.
phases.commit: feat(api): establish validated authenticated service contracts

phases.title: Authentication across web and Android
steps: Implement the selected initial sign-up/sign-in method with Supabase Auth, verified callbacks, and recovery journeys.
Use secure native token storage and a reviewed web session strategy; implement refresh, expiry, logout, and device state clearing.
Add understandable pending/error states, email link handling, and abuse controls without requesting unrelated permissions.
acceptance: A user can sign up, verify, sign in, recover access, and sign out on each platform.
Private routes and local cached content are hidden or cleared according to the session policy.
Expired/revoked sessions stop synchronization and do not silently discard offline drafts.
checks: Test callback replay/invalid links, expiry, logout, browser tab behavior, and Android process restart.
Review session token locations and CSRF/XSS assumptions.
phases.commit: feat(auth): add secure web and Android account journeys

phases.title: Personal workspace and preferences
steps: Create exactly one initial private workspace through an idempotent provision flow.
Store user time zone, locale, week start, display preferences, and workspace membership context.
Define preference versioning and account/workspace boundaries that later sharing can extend.
acceptance: Repeated provisioning cannot duplicate the personal workspace.
Clients cannot select a workspace without current membership.
Time zone and week-start preferences survive re-login and have explicit defaults.
checks: Test concurrent provisioning, stale membership, preference validation, and cross-tenant IDs.
Run sign-in to workspace selection journeys on web and Android.
phases.commit: feat(workspaces): add personal workspace and user preferences

phases.title: Local data repositories and migrations
steps: Implement encrypted SQLite and reviewed native key wrapping on mobile after Phase 03 proves support; implement IndexedDB on web with explicit trusted-device persistence consent, opt-out, and clear-data controls. Store item headers, drafts, pending mutations, cursors, and preference snapshots.
Define local schema migrations and account-scoped namespaces; add transaction-safe write/read operations.
Expose persistence failures and storage quota conditions without showing a false saved state.
acceptance: Drafts survive app/process restart and normal offline navigation.
Signing into another account cannot display previous account content.
Interrupted migration either finishes safely or returns a documented recovery path.
Native cached ordinary data follows the reviewed encryption/key lifecycle; browser persistence requires deliberate consent and is never described as client-encrypted normal content.
checks: Test adapter contract parity, crash/restart, quota failure, and migration from a prior fixture.
Run real Android SQLite and browser IndexedDB persistence checks.
Test browser trusted-device refusal, clear-data/account switch, and native encryption key failure/reinstall; inspect raw local storage with synthetic data.
phases.commit: feat(storage): add account-scoped local persistence adapters

phases.title: Server mutation receipts and change feed
steps: Implement idempotent mutation IDs, optimistic revisions, transactional receipt/outbox persistence, and tenant-scoped changes.
Design commit-safe feed cursor ordering that cannot skip later-committing transactions; document compaction and reset semantics.
Add tombstones, snapshot bootstrap, bounded pagination, and conflict responses with preserved server versions.
acceptance: Retrying a mutation returns its existing result without double creation.
Clients never acknowledge a cursor that can skip a committed change.
Expired cursors trigger a safe snapshot reset while keeping unsent local mutations.
checks: Test duplicate/concurrent requests, rollback, commit order races, pagination, and cursor expiration.
Run authorization tests for receipts, snapshots, and tombstones.
phases.commit: feat(sync): add durable mutation receipts and ordered changes

phases.title: Shared client synchronization engine
steps: Implement local transactional enqueue, retry with backoff, mutation acknowledgments, paginated pulls, and cancellation.
Handle auth loss, app resume, reconnect, multiple browser tabs, and cursor reset without erasing drafts.
Display local save and cloud sync status separately; add a safe diagnostic summary.
acceptance: Offline create/edit operations synchronize once after reconnect.
A lost response, killed process, or second browser tab does not duplicate work.
Conflict/error state is visible and unresolved content remains recoverable.
checks: Run shared state-machine and adapter integration tests with network fault injection.
Test airplane mode/restart/reconnect on Android and offline tabs in browser.
phases.commit: feat(sync): synchronize offline mutations across web and mobile

phases.title: Collections folders and shared item metadata
steps: Implement collection/folder creation, rename, move, order, archive, and item references within one workspace.
Reject cycles, unauthorized parents, invalid depth, and incompatible scopes transactionally.
Define move/delete semantics, Inbox defaults, tags, and item links without copying feature bodies.
acceptance: User-created folders can organize notes, tasks, journals, files, and later compatible types.
Cross-workspace references and folder cycles are rejected.
Deleting a folder follows a visible documented preservation/trash policy.
checks: Test deep trees, concurrent moves, revision conflicts, unauthorized parents, and trash behavior.
Measure indexed folder listing with large synthetic trees.
phases.commit: feat(organization): add workspace folders and common item metadata

phases.title: Folder browsing and organization interfaces
steps: Implement folder browsing, breadcrumbs, typed item lists, create/rename/move, and folder selection.
Provide reorder gestures plus keyboard/menu alternatives and explicit undo for reversible actions.
Add empty states, counts, loading/pagination, and offline status without exposing hidden modules.
acceptance: A user can create Software and Government Jobs folders and organize items inside each.
Move/reorder works with keyboard and TalkBack as well as pointer/touch.
Long names and large folders remain usable without blocking navigation.
checks: Run folder CRUD/move journeys across platforms and nested folder accessibility checks.
Verify offline changes and concurrent folder movement messages.
phases.commit: feat(library): add accessible folder browsing and organization

phases.title: Typed note domain and persistence
steps: Implement titled typed notes with plain text and safe constrained formatting, stable IDs, drafts, and revisions.
Support folder placement, tags, pin, archive, trash, and server/local validation.
Choose a portable versioned document format; sanitize rendered text and preserve line breaks and Unicode.
acceptance: Notes persist and participate in folder organization and offline sync.
Formatting contains no executable HTML and exported text remains portable.
Revision conflicts preserve both draft and server content.
checks: Test note invariants, Unicode/long content, malicious markup, permissions, and retry behavior.
Round-trip portable note documents through local/server persistence.
phases.commit: feat(notes): add portable typed notes and draft persistence

phases.title: Focused note editor on both platforms
steps: Add distraction-free title/body editing, autosave feedback, folder selection, and a restrained formatting toolbar.
Keep keyboard focus stable and preserve selection while saving.
Add unsaved/failure/conflict recovery and accessible note actions; do not mix audio capture into typed note creation.
acceptance: The user can type, close, reopen, and find the same note without an explicit save ritual.
Editor handles long text and native/browser keyboards comfortably.
The UI distinguishes local persistence from cloud synchronization.
checks: Test restart during typing, offline edits, navigation while saving, and failed persistence.
Review typing responsiveness and text scaling with real devices and browser assistive technology.
phases.commit: feat(notes): deliver focused web and mobile note editors

phases.title: Upcoming task domain and deadlines
steps: Implement task title, optional details, priority, status, deadline semantics, completion, and folder links.
Separate date-only deadlines from timed due instants and define overdue boundaries in the user's zone.
Support subtasks and deterministic sorting; keep daily routines as a distinct domain.
acceptance: Priority and deadline filters produce stable results.
Completion records an instant and reopening retains task history.
Timed and date-only deadlines behave correctly across time zones.
checks: Test overdue transitions, leap days/DST, completion retries, priorities, and authorization.
Test parent/subtask invariants and folder consistency.
phases.commit: feat(tasks): add prioritized tasks and explicit deadline semantics

phases.title: Upcoming task lists and detail views
steps: Build upcoming, overdue, and completed views with priority indicators, sort/filter controls, and task details.
Add quick task capture, subtasks, deadline editing, accessible completion, and undo.
Keep daily routine navigation separate and avoid filling the initial view with advanced filters.
acceptance: A task can be created, prioritized, scheduled, completed, reopened, and moved to a folder.
Overdue state is explained using text and dates rather than color alone.
Bulk actions are confirmable and cannot silently affect hidden selections.
checks: Run end-to-end task journeys on web and Android with offline operation.
Review keyboard, TalkBack, large text, and date-picker behavior.
phases.commit: feat(tasks): add upcoming task workflows and priority views

phases.title: Daily routine schedules and occurrences
steps: Implement daily/selected-weekday routine templates with active periods and an explicit scheduling time zone.
Create date-scoped occurrence identities with completion/skipped state and idempotent generation.
Define schedule edits, travel/time zone changes, history retention, and missed-day behavior without resetting prior records.
acceptance: Completing today's routine never completes tomorrow's occurrence.
Repeated generation cannot duplicate one scheduled occurrence.
Editing a template preserves completed history and applies the documented future rule.
checks: Test midnight, DST/travel, schedule edits, concurrent completion, and occurrence uniqueness.
Validate behavior when a device stays offline for several days.
phases.commit: feat(routines): add date-scoped daily routine occurrences

phases.title: Daily routine experience and history
steps: Build today's routine checklist, routine creation/editing, pause, skip, and history.
Offer gentle progress with no punitive streak dependency or forced notifications.
Show why a routine is due today and how changes affect future dates.
acceptance: Users can complete daily work independently from upcoming tasks.
Yesterday's completion remains visible while today starts a new occurrence.
Paused routines and skipped days have clear understandable states.
checks: Run multi-day/time-zone journeys with fake clocks and real local adapters.
Review low-friction checklist use with screen readers and undo.
phases.commit: feat(routines): add daily checklists and completion history

phases.title: Journal entries and privacy defaults
steps: Implement dated entries with title/body, optional mood/tags/prompts, multiple entries per day, and collection placement.
Keep journal private by default and separate its date semantics from server created timestamps.
Add draft/version handling, edit history policy, and non-clinical optional reflection templates.
acceptance: Entries can be browsed by local date and organized in user folders.
Mood and prompts remain optional with no forced scoring.
Journal content is omitted from operational telemetry and sharing defaults.
checks: Test backdating, multiple entries per day, privacy, offline drafts, and Unicode.
Verify journal body does not enter API logs or analytics.
phases.commit: feat(journal): add private dated entries and optional reflection metadata

phases.title: Journal writing and reflection interfaces
steps: Create a calm writing canvas, optional prompt tray, mood input, draft recovery, and dated timeline.
Add day/month browse and search entry points with meaningful empty states.
Support folders/templates without crowding the editor; hide journal body previews on Today and notifications by default, and honor timeline/search snippet preferences.
acceptance: The user can start an entry in a few actions, write freely, and revisit a date.
Prompts can be dismissed and no journal action automatically sends content to AI.
Long sessions survive interruption with a visible recoverable draft.
checks: Run interrupted writing, backdated entry, timeline, and privacy preview journeys.
Review comfort, text hierarchy, large text, keyboard behavior, and TalkBack.
phases.commit: feat(journal): add focused writing and reflection journeys

phases.title: Private binary upload lifecycle
steps: Implement authorized upload reservations, quota checks, provider-expiring signed upload capabilities, completion verification, and item linking. Return actual provider expiry (Supabase upload URLs are documented as two hours) rather than claiming a configurable five-minute upload lifetime.
Quarantine untrusted files, verify declared/actual type and size, and add malware scanning policy before share/preview.
Add idempotent finalize, orphan cleanup, deletion jobs, immutable versions, and resumable/retry behavior where supported.

Bound temporary/orphan storage before issuing capabilities: prove a per-upload byte bound or reserve the maximum the provider capability can accept, limit outstanding reservations, and reconcile after capability expiry; finalize-only quota checks are insufficient.
acceptance: A binary becomes available only after ownership, integrity, size, and safety checks.
Guessing object paths cannot download another workspace's files.
Interrupted uploads and retries cannot create unlimited orphan storage or bypass quota.
checks: Test wrong MIME/size, malicious filename, quota races, missing objects, duplicate finalize, and unauthorized reads.
Run failed-upload and cleanup job fault-injection tests.
Attempt a larger-than-declared upload through the raw signed capability, concurrent reservations, and writes before capability expiry; prove temporary storage remains within enforced exposure limits.
phases.commit: feat(files): add private verified uploads and storage lifecycle

phases.title: Files folders and safe previews
steps: Add device/browser upload, progress/retry/cancel, file detail, folder placement, and authorized download.
Provide safe image/PDF previews; show metadata/download for unsupported office documents without claiming full editing.
Make availability, storage usage, and cloud/offline status visible; let users choose downloads for offline access.
acceptance: Users can upload PDF/image/document files into their own Software and Government Jobs folders.
Cancelled, rejected, or offline uploads have actionable states.
Preview and cached downloads respect account boundaries and cleanup policy.
checks: Test representative image/PDF/office files, large/empty files, cancel/retry, and expired read links.
Review preview sandboxing, accessibility, and physical-device file picker behavior.
phases.commit: feat(files): add organized uploads and safe document previews

phases.title: Calendar and deadline views
steps: Build a read model for upcoming task deadlines and scheduled routine occurrences without duplicating task records.
Implement agenda/day/month views, date navigation, zone/week-start preferences, and accessible list alternatives.
Add personal calendar events with separate date-only/timed semantics: all-day intervals use exclusive end dates and timed end must follow start. Keep external calendar integration outside this phase.
Implement authorized event create/read/update/trash, local adapter persistence, sync projections, and migrations. Add optional journal-date indicators without entry body exposure.
acceptance: Upcoming tasks appear on their due date and link back to the source task.
Changing a deadline updates all views through one domain record.
Users can read calendar content without interpreting a visual grid.
checks: Test DST/month boundaries, date-only deadlines, long-range pagination, and duplicate source prevention.
Run web/Android agenda and month navigation journeys.
Test event CRUD and offline/reconnect round trips, interval validation, cross-tenant access, journal indicator privacy, and calendar schema upgrade fixtures.
phases.commit: feat(calendar): add linked deadlines routines and personal events

phases.title: Reminder scheduling and durable delivery jobs
steps: Implement reminder preferences, schedule versioning, recurrence instances, snooze, quiet hours, and cancellation.
Use transactional outbox and durable leased jobs with retry/deduplication; separate device schedules from server delivery.
Invalidate old schedules when tasks complete or dates/zones change and record operational delivery status without sensitive bodies.
acceptance: Completing/rescheduling a task invalidates its stale pending reminder.
Retrying a delivery job does not create duplicate reminder instances.
Reminder status distinguishes scheduled/provider-accepted from observed/user-opened and never guarantees receipt.
checks: Test leased-job crash recovery, duplicate deliveries, snooze, quiet hours, DST, and schedule edits.
Verify redacted payloads and unauthorized reminder targets.
phases.commit: feat(reminders): add durable scheduling and delivery state

phases.title: Android notifications and local reminders
steps: Add contextual notification permission requests, channel preferences, device token rotation, local schedules, and push fallback.
Coordinate local/server delivery by reminder instance identity and rebuild schedules after edits/resume/reboot as supported.
Handle notification deep links and redacted lock-screen previews; implement exact audible alarms only if the earlier policy/native feasibility gate permits, otherwise retain ordinary reminders.
acceptance: Permission refusal leaves tasks usable and settings explain actual delivery capability.
A reminder opens its authorized task and stale reminders are cancelled.
Physical-device evidence covers background/reboot/power-saving constraints with honest timing copy.
checks: Test granted/denied/revoked permission, token change, offline schedules, reboot, task completion, and duplicate local/push paths.
Record exact-alarm eligibility outcome separately; no exact timing acceptance is implied.
phases.commit: feat(notifications): add Android reminder delivery and permission controls

phases.title: Web reminder delivery and PWA support
steps: Implement supported-browser Web Push subscription lifecycle and contextual permission controls.
Add a reviewed PWA shell/offline cache strategy excluding private API responses and secrets from shared caches.
Provide in-app reminder/agenda fallback and capability messaging where notifications or persistent background operation are unavailable.
acceptance: Supported browsers receive an authorized notification with a safe deep link.
Private account data never leaks through shared service-worker/CDN caching.
Unsupported or denied notification environments remain useful and do not promise browser alarms.
checks: Test subscription expiry/revoke, account logout, service-worker upgrade, offline shell, and shared-computer behavior.
Review actual supported browser/device matrix rather than claiming universal PWA behavior.
phases.commit: feat(web): add browser reminders and reviewed offline shell

phases.title: Today home and personal customization
steps: Combine today's routine occurrences, upcoming priorities, recent items, and quick capture in a calm configurable home.
Support section hide/show, rename labels, favorite folders, widget ordering, density, and theme with restore defaults.
Keep personalization as versioned user layout metadata; do not generate executable UI or expose every future feature.
acceptance: A new account shows a small useful default home.
Users can rearrange widgets with touch/pointer and accessible move controls.
Hidden content remains discoverable through Library and layout resets preserve user data.
checks: Test cross-device layout sync/conflicts, missing modules, restore defaults, and keyboard reordering.
Review home usability at compact/wide widths with realistic synthetic data.
phases.commit: feat(home): add a customizable daily organizer dashboard

phases.title: First-use tutorial and progressive discovery
steps: Add a short skippable first-sign-in tutorial with selected goals/modules and an initial folder/example action.
Teach capture, organization, daily versus upcoming work, and personalization at the moment of use.
Persist onboarding progress, allow replay in Settings, and defer microphone/notification/Drive prompts until their features are invoked.
acceptance: New users can reach a useful home without completing every tutorial step.
Skipping/replaying never duplicates folders or removes content.
Advanced features appear through deliberate enablement and contextual guidance.
checks: Run fresh account, interrupted onboarding, skip/replay, and multi-device journeys.
Review screen-reader focus, copy comprehension, and completion friction with pilot users.
phases.commit: feat(onboarding): guide first use with progressive feature discovery

phases.title: Knowledge guides and cheatsheet organization
steps: Add a knowledge collection preset for typed guides/cheatsheets using the existing note format and folders.
Support pins, tags, safe internal item links/backlinks, and saved filters without duplicating note bodies.
Provide quick-reference browsing and copyable text/code blocks with clear text-only capture boundaries.
acceptance: A user can maintain guides and cheatsheets inside custom topic folders.
An item has one canonical body even if shown in several saved views.
Links validate workspace access and unavailable targets are explained.
checks: Test saved-view queries, backlinks, move/delete targets, and cross-tenant link rejection.
Review quick-reference use and accessibility on small and wide displays.
phases.commit: feat(knowledge): add organized guides cheatsheets and saved views

phases.title: Global authorized search and filters
steps: Implement PostgreSQL full-text/trigram search over allowed plain content and metadata with type/folder/date filters.
Add account-scoped local search for downloaded items with explicitly limited offline coverage.
Exclude vault ciphertext and enforce current authorization before returning snippets or counts.
acceptance: Search finds notes, task titles, journal entries, and file metadata the user can access.
No unauthorized content or count leaks through global search.
Results state offline coverage and allow clear context-aware navigation.
checks: Test permissions, injection-like input, deleted items, pagination, and multilingual content.
Measure indexed search with the documented synthetic dataset.
phases.commit: feat(search): add permission-scoped organizer search

phases.title: Conflict recovery and offline hardening
steps: Add side-by-side conflict review with keep-both/choose-version behavior for text and explicit policies for structured fields.
Harden deleted-parent references, account switching, cursor reset, storage eviction, and partial attachment transfer.
Add local recovery export and a redacted sync diagnostic view without sending content automatically.
acceptance: Concurrent editing never silently destroys either text version.
A reconnect after long offline use preserves queued mutations or gives a recoverable explanation.
Users can distinguish storage failure, conflict, and network delay.
checks: Run multi-device concurrent-edit/delete, crash/restart, cursor compaction, and quota/eviction fault tests.
Inspect recovery usability with realistic lost-network scenarios.
phases.commit: fix(sync): preserve edits through conflicts and offline failures

phases.title: Portable export and controlled import
steps: Require recent supported reauthentication before creating a protected workspace export; export metadata and typed content in documented JSON/Markdown/CSV formats with selected binary files and a manifest.
Implement validated bounded import with preview, duplicate mapping, schema versions, and safe path handling.
Use authorized expiring download links and communicate that vault/Drive external content require separate policies.
acceptance: An exported core workspace can be imported into a clean test account with preserved meaningful content.
Malformed archives, traversal paths, oversize entries, and duplicate imports fail safely.
Users understand which remote/undownloaded files and later vault content are included.
checks: Run round-trip fixtures including Unicode, folders, tasks, routines, journal, and attachment references.
Test archive safety, expiration, authorization, cancellation, and quota enforcement.
Test recent-reauthentication expiry/cancellation, session binding, and unauthorized export link reuse.
phases.commit: feat(portability): add documented workspace export and import

phases.title: Account deletion backup and recovery lifecycle
steps: Require recent supported reauthentication and explicit confirmation for account/workspace deletion; implement token revocation, local removal, queued blob deletion, cancellation of connectors/reminders, and honest retention disclosure.
Configure database and object backup strategy separately and perform a staging restore drill.
Document provider disconnect, shared-content ownership, outstanding drafts, backup retention, and incident recovery procedures.
acceptance: Deleted users cannot continue accessing data or reminder subscriptions.
A restore drill proves recovery of both metadata and included object versions.
Deletion states, backup exceptions, and recovery retention are explained without false immediate-erasure promises.
checks: Test deletion retries, orphan objects, revoked sessions/devices, cancelled jobs, and multi-device local clearing.
Record backup restore evidence and primary Play account-deletion policy review.
Test cancelled/expired/replayed deletion reauthentication and server-bound confirmation state.
phases.commit: feat(privacy): add account deletion and verified recovery procedures

phases.title: Core quality and usability release gate
steps: Exercise complete personal organizer journeys across browser and physical Android devices using realistic synthetic data.
Audit accessibility, localization readiness, permission boundaries, file safety, migration behavior, and recovery.
Measure performance and run a small usability study; fix gate failures within this bounded phase or split concrete defect phases before release.
acceptance: Core acceptance scenarios and cross-tenant negative tests pass with recorded evidence.
No unresolved critical/high security or data-loss defects remain.
Documented performance targets are measured and accessibility review has no blocking failures.
checks: Run the full core scenario suite, migration/restore tests, security review, and documented load/device checks.
Record pilot usability observations and resolved defects without inventing satisfaction metrics.
phases.commit: test(core): verify organizer quality and release readiness

phases.title: Controlled private beta
steps: Prepare isolated staging/beta environments, limited access, feature flags, rollback, redacted monitoring, and support feedback flow.
Produce signed internal Android builds and a private web beta; deployment and account prerequisites require the owner's authorized target.
Run an agreed beta observation period and triage findings into bounded follow-up phases before widening access.
acceptance: Only intended testers can access the beta and visible features match shipped scope.
Rollback and operational alert routes are exercised.
Beta evidence names unresolved issues and does not label the app publicly production-ready.
checks: Run deployed smoke tests, signed-build installation, auth callbacks, reminders, and restoration drills.
Record user/device coverage and feedback actions; if external prerequisites are missing, keep the gate pending.
phases.commit: chore(beta): prepare and validate the private organizer release

phases.title: Expense tracking domain
steps: Implement manual expense/income/refund records, user categories, dates, notes, optional receipt references, and folder organization. A refund references an original expense, uses its currency, and reduces spending rather than increasing income; partial refunds cannot cumulatively exceed the original without a later reviewed policy.
Store money as integer minor units with currency metadata and explicit precision; do not sum unrelated currencies.
Add recurring entry templates and month totals without bank linking, tax claims, or financial advice.

Define transaction-date reporting for refunds, category inheritance, reversal/edit/trash constraints, and original-expense deletion before writing migrations; defer account transfers unless separately specified.
acceptance: Amounts round-trip accurately without floating-point drift.
Totals are grouped by currency and local date boundaries.
Receipts remain governed by the file access policy and private by default.
checks: Test zero/negative/currency precision rules, category deletion, date boundaries, and receipt permissions.
